question: Who introduced the law that abolished the practice of Sati in British India in 1829?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord William Bentinck**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Lord William Bentinck**, who served as the **Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835**, introduced the law that abolished the practice of Sati in British India. 
 
• The practice of Sati involved the **self-immolation of widows on the funeral pyres of their deceased husbands**. It was considered a social evil and was prevalent in certain parts of India. 
 
• On **December 4, 1829**, Lord William Bentinck passed the **Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829**, which declared the practice of Sati as **illegal and punishable by criminal courts**. 
 
• The regulation applied initially to the **Bengal Presidency** but was later extended to other regions of British India. 
 
• This decision was supported by prominent social reformers like **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, who actively campaigned against Sati and advocated for women's rights in India. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy:** 
 
 
• He was a prominent **social reformer** during the 19th century in India and played a key role in the abolition of Sati. 
 
• He founded the **Brahmo Samaj** in 1828, which aimed to reform Hindu society by eliminating practices like Sati, child marriage, and caste discrimination. 
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy also argued that the practice of Sati was not mandated by Hindu scriptures and was against the principles of humanity. 
 
 
 
• **Lord William Bentinck's Reforms:** 
 
 
• In addition to abolishing Sati, Lord William Bentinck introduced several other reforms during his tenure as Governor-General. 
 
• He worked on improving **education** by promoting English as the medium of instruction and supporting missionary schools. 
 
• He also reformed the judicial system by introducing measures to curb corruption and ensure fairness in the administration of justice. 
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Abolition of Sati:** 
 
 
• The abolition of Sati was a **landmark reform** that marked the beginning of a series of social changes in India during British rule. 
 
• It set a precedent for future reforms targeting other social evils, such as child marriage and untouchability. 
 
• Although there was some opposition to the law, it was widely regarded as a progressive step towards gender equality and women's empowerment. 
 
 
 
• **Other British Governors-General:** 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie:** Known for his policies of annexation, such as the Doctrine of Lapse, and his role in modernizing India with the introduction of railways, telegraphs, and postal systems. 
 
• **Lord Curzon:** Remembered for the partition of Bengal in 1905 and his efforts to preserve Indian heritage through the Archaeological Survey of India. 
 
• **Lord Canning:** Served as the first Viceroy of India after the Revolt of 1857 and was instrumental in implementing the Government of India Act of 1858. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829:** 
 
 
• This legislation was one of the first significant steps taken by the British to address social issues in India. 
 
• The regulation explicitly stated that all cases of Sati would be treated as culpable homicide. 
 
 
 
• **Role of Public Opinion:** 
 
 
• The abolition of Sati received support from certain sections of Indian society, including intellectuals and reformers, but faced resistance from conservative groups. 
 
• The British justified the law as part of their civilizing mission in India. 
 
 
 
• **Global Context:** 
 
 
• The abolition of Sati can be seen within the broader context of 19th-century movements for social reform and human rights worldwide.
